examples.en: The speaker is too loud.
I played music through the speaker.
I bought a new Bluetooth speaker.

examples.ko: 스피커가 고장 났는지 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: The speaker seems broken, since there is no sound.
I connect my phone to the speaker.

examples.ko: 스피커는 방 구석에 두는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is better to put the speaker in a corner of the room.

explain: '스피커폰으로 통화하다'처럼 전화 소리를 밖으로 내는 기능에도 써요. 이어폰은 귀에 꽂고, 스피커는 밖으로 소리를 내요.

phrases.en: Can I talk on speakerphone?
phrases.nuance_ko: 전화 소리를 밖으로 내는 기능을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The function that plays a call's sound out loud.

phrases.en: I listen to music on a Bluetooth speaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선 없이 연결하는 스피커예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A speaker that connects without a wire.

phrases.en: Please turn on the speaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 내게 할 때 '켜다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with 켜다 to turn the sound on.

explain_en: Device that plays sound, like music or announcements. It is also used for the phone function that plays call sound aloud, as in 'seupikeophoneuro tonghwahada'. Earphones go in your ears; a speaker sends sound out into the room.

examples.en: There is trust between us.

examples.ko: 신뢰를 얻으려면 약속을 잘 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: To earn trust you have to keep your promises.

examples.ko: 작은 거짓말 하나로 신뢰에 금이 갔어요.
examples.en: One small lie put a crack in the trust.

examples.ko: 한 번 깨진 신뢰는 다시 쌓기 어려워요.
examples.en: Trust that has been broken once is hard to rebuild.

examples.ko: 신뢰할 수 있는 사람과 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with someone I can trust.
Friendships are held together by trust.

explain: '믿음'과 뜻이 가깝지만, 신뢰는 회사·뉴스·정치처럼 조금 딱딱한 자리에서 더 잘 써요. 친구나 가족에게는 '믿음'이나 '믿다'를 더 자주 말해요. '신뢰를 얻다', '신뢰를 쌓다', '신뢰가 깨지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 정해져 있어요.

phrases.en: I build trust by keeping even small promises.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간이 지나면서 조금씩 믿음을 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means gradually building trust over time.

phrases.en: Trust is broken when you lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿음이 없어졌을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when trust is lost.

phrases.en: I trust that doctor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '믿다'보다 딱딱한 동사로, 사람이나 회사에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal verb than 믿다, used for people or companies.

explain_en: General trust between people or in things. It is close to 믿음, but 신뢰 suits slightly stiff settings such as business, news, and politics. With friends and family, people more often say 믿음 or 믿다. It pairs with fixed verbs: 신뢰를 얻다, 신뢰를 쌓다, 신뢰가 깨지다.

examples.en: I went to watch an ice hockey game in winter.

examples.ko: 아이스하키는 얼음 위에서 퍽을 쳐서 해요.
examples.en: In ice hockey, you hit a puck on the ice.
My younger sibling is learning ice hockey.
Ice hockey is fun, so I watch it every week.
Everyone cheered when a goal was scored in the ice hockey game.
I am trying both ice hockey and skating for the first time.

explain: '하키'만 말하면 땅 위에서 하는 필드하키를 뜻할 수 있어서, 얼음 위에서 하는 경기는 앞에 '아이스'를 붙여요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is an ice hockey player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이 운동을 직업이나 취미로 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who plays the sport, professionally or for fun.

phrases.en: I play ice hockey with friends every winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이름 뒤에 '하다'를 붙여 직접 한다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 하다 after a sport name means playing it.

phrases.en: The ice hockey rink is very cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-장'은 장소를 뜻해서 경기를 하는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -장 means a place, so this is where the game is played.

explain_en: Saying 하키 alone can mean the field version played on grass, so the game on ice gets 아이스 in front.

en: front view; the way someone looks from the front

examples.ko: 나가기 전에 거울로 내 앞모습을 확인했어요.
examples.en: Before going out, I checked my front view in the mirror.

examples.ko: 앞모습은 멋있는데 뒷모습은 어딘가 피곤해 보여요.
examples.en: He looks cool from the front, but from behind he looks somehow tired.

examples.ko: 사진 속 앞모습만 보고는 누군지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I couldn't tell who it was just from the front view in the photo.
From the front, he looks a lot like his father.
The front of the building was pretty, so I took a photo.

examples.ko: 뒷모습만 보고 아는 사람인 줄 알았는데 앞모습을 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I thought it was someone I knew from the back, but I was startled when I saw the front.

explain: 반대말은 '뒷모습'이에요. 사람의 얼굴이나 앞쪽 모양, 건물의 앞쪽 모양에 써요. '뒷모습'은 쓸쓸하거나 믿음직한 느낌을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That building looks really great from the front.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 본 모양이 보기 좋을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the front view looks good.
phrases.en_equiv: to look good from the front

phrases.en: I took a photo of my friend from the front.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정면에서 사진을 찍는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes taking a photo from the front.

phrases.en: I checked how I look from the front in the mirror.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정면의 모습을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking how you look from the front.

explain_en: The opposite is '뒷모습' (back view). It is used for a person's face or front appearance and for the front of a building. '뒷모습' is often used to describe a lonely or reliable feeling.

examples.en: Palm trees stand in a row on the beach.
I rested for a moment in the shade of a palm tree.
They planted palm trees in the hotel garden.
The palm leaves are swaying in the wind.
Many palm trees grow in tropical regions.

examples.ko: 그림 속 야자수가 휴양지 느낌을 줘요.
examples.en: The palm tree in the picture gives a resort feel.

explain: '야자나무'라고도 해요. 야자수는 바다, 휴가, 열대 같은 느낌을 떠올리게 해서 그림이나 인테리어에서도 자주 쓰여요.

phrases.en: There is a big palm tree in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야자수와 같은 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 'yajasu'.

phrases.example: 야자수 길을 따라 걸으면 휴가 온 기분이에요.
phrases.en: Walking along the palm tree road feels like being on vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야자수가 늘어선 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a road lined with palm trees.

phrases.en: We took photos under a palm tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a location.

explain_en: It is also called '야자나무'. Palm trees bring to mind the sea, vacations and the tropics, so they are often used in pictures and interior decoration.

t90.ax: Palm trees stand in a row on the beach.

examples.en: I stuffed some clothes loosely into the travel bag.
Clothes are scattered on the floor.

examples.ko: 이사하기 전에 안 입는 옷가지를 정리했어요.
examples.en: Before moving, I sorted out the clothes I don't wear.
I grabbed just a few pieces of clothing and left.
Please bring me the clothes to wash.
I dry clothes soaked by rain separately.

explain: '옷' 한 벌이 아니라 이것저것 여러 종류의 옷을 가볍게 묶어 말할 때 써요. '옷가지 몇 벌'처럼 말하고, 옷 하나를 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않아요. 짐을 싸거나 빨래, 정리할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I packed some clothes before the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짐을 쌀 때 필요한 옷을 모으는 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gathering needed clothes when packing.

phrases.en: I sorted my clothes over the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 옷을 한꺼번에 정돈할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for tidying many pieces of clothing at once.

phrases.en: I folded the clothes I had washed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨래한 여러 옷을 접어 정리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for folding a mixed pile of washed clothes.

explain_en: Collective term for a few assorted pieces of clothing, e.g. what you pack (옷가지를 챙기다) Use it to loosely group several pieces of clothing, not one garment. You say things like '옷가지 몇 벌', and you don't use it for a single item. It often comes up when packing, doing laundry or tidying.

t90.ax: Clothes are scattered on the floor.

examples.en: In autumn the ginkgo leaves turn yellow.
I walked stepping on the ginkgo leaves piled on the ground.
I made a bookmark out of a ginkgo leaf.
The color of the ginkgo leaves is really pretty.
A ginkgo leaf is shaped like a fan.
Sunlight shines on the yellow ginkgo leaves and it's dazzling.

explain: '은행'은 은행나무와 열매를 가리키기도 하고 'bank'와 소리가 같지만, 문맥으로 쉽게 구분돼요. 가을 단풍 이야기에서 '노란 은행잎'이 자주 나와요. [은행닙]으로 발음해요.

phrases.en: The road is full of yellow ginkgo leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을 풍경을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing when describing autumn scenery.

phrases.en: When the wind blew, the ginkgo leaves fell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가을에 잎이 지는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe leaves falling in autumn.

phrases.en: I picked up ginkgo leaves with my child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅에 떨어진 잎을 집을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when picking up leaves from the ground.

explain_en: '은행' can mean the ginkgo tree and its nut, and it sounds like 'bank', but the context makes it easy to tell. '노란 은행잎' (yellow ginkgo leaves) often comes up when talking about autumn colors. It is pronounced [은행닙].

examples.en: I feel deep respect for my parents.
My respect toward my teacher grew little by little.

examples.ko: 존경심은 말보다 행동으로 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You should show respect through actions rather than words.

examples.ko: 그는 존경심으로 가득한 눈으로 할아버지를 바라봤어요.
examples.en: He looked at his grandfather with eyes full of respect.
It was a small action that came from respect.
It is behavior with neither respect nor manners.

explain: '호기심', '애국심'처럼 '-심'은 마음을 나타내요. '존경심을 느끼다', '존경심을 갖다'처럼 써요. 사람을 대할 때는 '선생님을 존경해요'라고 동사로 말하고, 다른 사람의 의견이나 선택을 인정할 때는 '존중'을 써요.

phrases.en: I have respect for my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음속에 존경하는 마음이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for holding respect in your heart.

phrases.en: After hearing the story, I came to respect that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존경하는 마음이 새로 생길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when respect newly arises.

phrases.en: I respect my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 직접 말할 때는 동사 '존경하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a person, use the verb '존경하다'.

explain_en: Respect felt toward a person, such as a parent or teacher. As in '호기심' and '애국심', the '-심' part shows a feeling in the mind. It goes with '존경심을 느끼다' and '존경심을 갖다'. About a person you can use the verb, as in '선생님을 존경해요', and for accepting someone's opinion or choice you use '존중'.

t90.ax: I feel deep respect for my parents.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 편리성이 가장 큰 장점이에요.
examples.en: This app's biggest strength is its convenience.
If you only consider convenience, a card is better than cash.
I think convenience is more important than price.

examples.ko: 온라인 쇼핑의 편리성 덕분에 시장에 잘 안 가요.
examples.en: Thanks to the convenience of online shopping, I rarely go to the market.
The convenience is good, but the price is too high.
You have to take care of both convenience and safety.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '편해요'나 '편리해요'라고 말하고, '편리성'은 제품이나 서비스를 비교하거나 설명할 때 써요. '-성'이 붙은 말이라 '안전성', '효율성'과 함께 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 앱은 편리성이 높아서 인기가 많아요.
phrases.en: This app is popular because it is very convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제품이나 서비스가 얼마나 편한지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how convenient a product or service is.

phrases.en: I care about convenience more than price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 고를 때 편한지를 중요하게 본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you give importance to convenience when choosing.

phrases.en: The subway is close, so it is really convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '편리성'보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, this is used more than 편리성.

explain_en: Quality of being convenient, used for products and apps. In everyday talk people say '편해요' or '편리해요', while '편리성' is used when comparing or describing products and services. It ends in '-성', so it often appears alongside words like '안전성' (safety) and '효율성' (efficiency).

t90.ax: This app's biggest strength is its convenience.

examples.en: If you read a lot of books, your expressive ability grows.

examples.ko: 한국어 표현력을 키우고 싶어서 일기를 써요.
examples.en: I want to build my Korean expression skills, so I write a diary.

examples.ko: 표현력은 연습하면 누구나 좋아질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can get better at expressing themselves with practice.
To give a good presentation, expressive skill matters too.
I was surprised by the child's expressive ability.

examples.ko: 저는 표현력과 이해력을 함께 기르고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to develop both expressiveness and comprehension.

explain: '표현력이 좋다', '표현력이 풍부하다', '표현력이 늘다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말 '어휘력'은 아는 단어의 양에 가깝고, '표현력'은 생각이나 느낌을 말과 글로 잘 나타내는 힘이에요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 표현력이 좋아서 이야기를 재미있게 해요.
phrases.en: That friend is good at expressing things, so they tell stories in an interesting way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 느낌을 말과 글로 잘 나타내는 사람에게 쓰는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment for someone who can put thoughts and feelings into words well.

phrases.en: This actor is very expressive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표현하는 방법이 다양하고 깊을 때 써요. '좋다'보다 더 구체적으로 칭찬하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone has varied and deep ways of expressing; a more specific compliment than '좋다'.

phrases.en: I write every day to build my expressive ability.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력해서 표현력을 더 좋게 만든다는 뜻이에요. 공부 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means working to improve your expressive ability; common when talking about study.

explain_en: It goes with phrases like '표현력이 좋다' and '표현력이 늘다'. The related word '어휘력' is closer to how many words you know, while '표현력' is how well you put thoughts and feelings into speech or writing.

examples.en: Korean has many ways of expressing politeness.

examples.ko: 같은 뜻도 표현법에 따라 느낌이 달라요.
examples.en: Even the same meaning feels different depending on how it is expressed.
I learned ways to express feelings from this book.
Ways of greeting differ a little from country to country.

examples.ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 공손한 표현법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me a polite way to ask for a favor.
Please explain it again in simpler words.

explain: '표현'이 말이나 글로 나타낸 것 자체라면, '표현법'은 그것을 나타내는 방식을 말해요. '감정 표현법', '인사 표현법'처럼 앞에 주제를 붙여서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I want to learn how to express feelings in Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 주제를 붙여 어떤 표현의 방식인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A topic word in front shows what kind of expression it is.

phrases.en: Ways of greeting differ depending on the situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인사를 어떻게 말하는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain how to say greetings.

phrases.en: Korean has many ways to show respect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표현하는 방식이 여러 가지라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there are many ways to express something.
phrases.en_equiv: to have various ways of expression

explain_en: While '표현' is the thing expressed itself, '표현법' is the way of expressing it. It is often used with a topic in front, like '감정 표현법' (ways to express feelings) or '인사 표현법' (ways to greet).

t90.ax: Please explain it again in simpler words.

examples.en: Small wildflowers have bloomed along the road.
The children picked wildflowers and made flower rings.
I felt spring in a tiny wildflower.
The walking path is full of wildflowers.

examples.ko: 풀꽃 이름을 하나도 몰라서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know any of the wildflower names, so I took photos.

examples.ko: 풀꽃은 작지만 자세히 보면 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: Wildflowers are small, but they are really pretty up close.

explain: 꽃집에서 파는 꽃이나 화단의 꽃과 달리, 들이나 길가에서 저절로 자라는 작은 꽃을 말할 때 써요. '들꽃'과 비슷하게 쓰지만 '풀꽃'은 풀처럼 작고 소박한 느낌이 더 있어요.

phrases.en: Many wildflowers bloomed along the mountain path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀꽃과 비슷하지만 들에 피는 꽃이라는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 풀꽃, but it feels more like flowers of the fields.

phrases.en: When spring comes, wildflowers start to bloom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃이 피는 모습을 말할 때 '피다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 피다 to talk about flowers blooming.

phrases.en: The small wildflowers by the road are pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀꽃의 작고 소박한 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Brings out the small, simple feeling of wildflowers.

explain_en: Native word; small humble flowers of grass, poetic feel. Unlike florist flowers or garden flowers, it refers to small flowers that grow by themselves in fields or by the road. It is close to '들꽃', but '풀꽃' sounds smaller and more modest, like the grass itself.
